reference.format: BF16 safetensors reference checkpoint; official model card recommends float32 on CPU and BF16 on non-CPU device.
reference.documented_outputs: typed answers, including P(yes) for noul, choice probabilities, spans/values/boxes; output_tokens=0
reference.documented_multi_question_limit: up to 16 questions packed in one forward pass in the ONNX card; reference checkpoint records d1_set_size=16
reference.query_conditioned_rerank_probe: One noul question per candidate image; state contains the user query and media contains the candidate pixels. Use the returned calibrated P(yes) only to rank the already retrieved candidates. No OCR, filename, answer label, or generated text score is supplied.

onnx.quantization: The official card describes q4 as mixed precision: selected MLP gate/up projections int4, other parts int8; paired q8 vision encoder. Not uniformly 4-bit.
onnx.runtime_finding: Static review of every Python source file at the pinned ONNX repo revision found the official SystemOne runner is still the Transformers/PyTorch implementation: runner.py imports torch, modeling_d1_lfm3_vl.py composes Lfm3SystemOne with the native PyTorch LFM3-VL model, and no Python source imports onnxruntime or constructs an InferenceSession. The official card documents the split graph I/O and processor configuration, but using ONNX Runtime for named questions would require a custom graph/preprocessing/readout adapter. No adapter or ONNX inference was attempted; the reference path is the bounded runtime proof.
onnx.macos_onnx_runtime: ONNX Runtime documents CoreMLExecutionProvider in official macOS Python wheels, but this does not establish that the d1 graph operators are placed on Core ML or that the d1 ONNX bundle runs on Apple GPU/ANE. No d1 graph/provider compatibility run was performed.
onnx.windows_status: The d1 ONNX card describes cross-platform ONNX Runtime and its q4 variant as CPU-targeted; Windows execution is documented/advertised but was not validated in this Mac experiment.
onnx.official_onnx_card_graph_io: Vision encoder produces projected image/video features; decoder consumes input_ids, attention_mask, position_ids, image_features/video_features, question_ids, and slot_positions and returns answer-slot logits plus final-norm hidden_states. One packed decoder row supports up to 16 questions.

review_notes.classification_probability: Use typed noul P(yes) for binary labels; use choice probabilities for content_type. Do not present these as user-facing confidence.
review_notes.retrieval_isolation: Candidate embeddings are generated by the existing normalized 768d EmbeddingGemma path. d1 receives only each raw candidate image and query text. Gold relevance remains in a separate scoring file.
review_notes.mac_and_windows: Mac results are actual measurements only after the authorized local run. Windows remains documented/runtime-path evidence, not a measured claim.
